# RLS / PLMD Authorization Guide

_Subtitle: Decision Support_
_Specialty: Sleep Medicine_
_onAppealLetter → /sleep/rls-plmd/appeal-letter_

## CPT Codes — RLS/PLMD Evaluation & Treatment

| CPT Code | Description | Auth Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 95810 | Polysomnography (PSG) — PLMD diagnosis | Often | PLMI ≥15 events/hour (adults) required for PLMD diagnosis |
| 99213–99215 | Office visit — E&M (sleep/neurology) | Rarely | Document IRLSS score, iron studies, prior treatment history |
| 96372 | Therapeutic injection (IV iron infusion) | Often | Ferric carboxymaltose (Injectafer) — ferritin <75 ng/mL |
| J1439 | Ferric carboxymaltose injection (Injectafer) | Often | STRONGLY RECOMMENDED per AASM 2024 CPG for iron-deficient RLS |
| J1436 | Ferric gluconate injection | Often | Alternative IV iron formulation |

## ICD-10-CM Diagnosis Codes

| ICD-10 | Description | Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G25.81 | Restless legs syndrome | Primary RLS diagnosis — most commonly used |
| G47.61 | Periodic limb movement disorder | PLMD confirmed on PSG (PLMI ≥15 events/hour) |
| G47.69 | Other sleep-related movement disorders | RLS/PLMD not otherwise specified |
| E61.1 | Iron deficiency | Comorbid iron deficiency driving RLS — code with G25.81 |
| N18.1–N18.9 | Chronic kidney disease | CKD-associated RLS (uremic RLS) — code as primary |
| O26.89 | Other specified pregnancy complications | RLS in pregnancy |

## AASM 2024 Update: Dopamine Agonist Augmentation Warning

**AASM 2024 CPG Change:** Pramipexole (Mirapex) and ropinirole (Requip) are now **CONDITIONALLY RECOMMENDED AGAINST** as first-line therapy for RLS due to augmentation risk.

**Augmentation** is defined as: symptoms worsening over time on dopamine agonist therapy, spreading to arms or trunk, occurring earlier in the day, or requiring dose escalation for the same effect. Prevalence: 8–68% of patients on long-term dopamine agonist therapy.

**Clinical implication for prior auth appeals:** If a payer requires a dopamine agonist trial before approving an alpha-2-delta ligand, cite AASM 2024 CPG and document that dopamine agonists are now conditionally recommended against due to augmentation risk. This is a valid medical exception to step therapy.

## Medication Prior Authorization Requirements

### Gabapentin Enacarbil (Horizant)
- RLS diagnosis (G25.81) with moderate-to-severe severity (IRLSS ≥11)
- Iron studies documented (ferritin, transferrin saturation)
- Step therapy: gabapentin or pregabalin trial often required by payers
- Renal function documented (contraindicated CrCl <30 mL/min)

**Common denial reason:** Step therapy not met, non-formulary, renal contraindication

### Pregabalin (Lyrica)
- RLS or PLMD diagnosis
- IRLSS score ≥11 or PSG-confirmed PLMI ≥15
- Iron deficiency addressed or ruled out
- Prior gabapentin trial often required

**Common denial reason:** Step therapy not met, Schedule V controlled substance restrictions

### IV Ferric Carboxymaltose (Injectafer)
- RLS diagnosis (G25.81)
- Serum ferritin <75 ng/mL OR ferritin <100 + transferrin sat <20%
- Oral iron trial failure or intolerance documentation
- AASM 2024 CPG: Strongly recommended for iron-deficient RLS

**Common denial reason:** Oral iron not tried, ferritin above payer threshold, non-formulary

## Documentation Checklist
- IRLSS (International Restless Legs Syndrome Study Group Rating Scale) score documented
- IRLSSG 5 essential diagnostic criteria met (urge to move, worsening at rest, relief with movement, evening/night predominance, not explained by another condition)
- PSG report with PLMI if PLMD diagnosis (PLMI ≥15 events/hour adults)
- Iron studies: serum ferritin and transferrin saturation
- Prior treatment history: alpha-2-delta ligands, dopamine agonists (with augmentation assessment)
- Renal function (eGFR) — required for gabapentin/pregabalin dosing
- Augmentation assessment if prior dopamine agonist use
- Comorbidities: CKD, pregnancy, depression, anxiety

## References
1. Trotti LM, et al. "Treatment of Restless Legs Syndrome and Periodic Limb Movement Disorder in Adults: An AASM Clinical Practice Guideline." J Clin Sleep Med. 2024.
2. Allen RP, et al. "Restless legs syndrome/Willis-Ekbom disease diagnostic criteria: updated IRLSSG consensus criteria." Sleep Med. 2014;15(8):860–873.
3. Garcia-Borreguero D, et al. "Guidelines for the first-line treatment of restless legs syndrome/Willis-Ekbom disease." Sleep Med. 2016;21:1–11.
4. AASM Practice Guidelines: aasm.org/clinical-resources/practice-standards/practice-guidelines/ (https://aasm.org/clinical-resources/practice-standards/practice-guidelines/)
